question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(x)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}14{p}^{4}-10{p}^{3}+5{p}^{2} & =2{p}^{4}+17{p}^{2} \\ 12{p}^{4}-10{p}^{3}+5{p}^{2} & =17{p}^{2} \\ 12{p}^{4}-10{p}^{3}-12{p}^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $2{p}^{2}.$ We can factor out the $2{p}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}12{p}^{4}-10{p}^{3}-12{p}^{2} & =0 \\ 2{p}^{2}(6{p}^{2}-5p-6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $6{p}^{2}-5p-6$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{p}^{2}(6{p}^{2}-5p-6) & =0 \\ 2{p}^{2}(3p+2)(2p-3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $p=0,$ $p=-\frac{2}{3},$ and $p=\frac{3}{2}.$
